title: eval-harness: add CI metrics hook + prompt-set regression quality gating
author: Ethan Park
description: Motivation: Reduce regressions caused by prompt-set changes and surface eval metrics directly in CI. This PR introduces a lightweight CI hook that runs the eval-harness prompt-set regression checks (per-prompt quality metrics) and publishes a summarized metrics payload to the CI job and Prometheus-compatible endpoint. The hook implements a configurable quality gate (thresholds per-metric) so PRs can fail fast on regressions and surface exact examples to reviewers. Changes include: 1) a new eval-harness CI hook script that runs selected prompt-sets in fast-mode and computes delta metrics; 2) integration with the existing Prometheus exporter so metrics appear in our internal dashboards; 3) added short-circuit gating logic and human-readable failure summaries to the GitHub workflow; 4) small additions to prompt_sets.yaml to declare stable gate sets; 5) end-to-end CI test to validate the hook. Commits are squashed on merge. This is backward-compatible: the hook is opt-in via workflow config and default thresholds are conservative. Linear refs ENG-4012 (quality-gate design) and ENG-3988 (CI integration). SUP-1241 tracked a customer incident that motivated lowering the detection latency for prompt regressions. Testing: unit tests for gating logic, integration test that runs a tiny prompt set, and a staged rollout on canary repo. Rollout: feature guarded; ops will enable the workflow on redwood and run in report-only mode for one week before enforcing. See release_notes for user-facing impact.
